name: andreea-product-composite

anchor.statement: A presenter is visibly shown holding a branded product packet in a sponsored advertisement interface.

claim: The image presents the visible presenter as holding and promoting the shown product packet.
hypothesis: A source comparison can determine whether the held product belongs to the depicted capture.
expected_information: A provenance-complete source comparison that tests the visible person-product relation.
exact_text: The reference is a separate clean product shot of the same packet design. It is likely a different original capture and does not establish whether the input image was edited.
assessment_rationale: A different original capture without a same-capture alteration baseline cannot establish that the visible held-product relation was composited.
discrepancy: The shown product packet was composited into the presenter's hand, materially fabricating the visible endorsement relation.

name: queen-coronation-bus-context

anchor.entity_name: queen figure on decorated double-decker bus
anchor.statement: A queen figure is visibly presented on the upper deck of a decorated double-decker bus marked with 1953 coronation text.

claim: The image presents Queen Elizabeth II as riding on the upper deck of the decorated 1953 coronation bus.
hypothesis: A historical source can establish who rode the decorated coronation bus and why it travelled to London.
expected_information: A fetched historical description that directly resolves the depicted queen-bus relation.
exact_text: Chesterfield Transport double decker bus decorated for the Coronation of Queen Elizabeth II in 1953 and used for a trip to London to see the occasion.
assessment_rationale: The fetched historical description identifies the vehicle as a decorated public trip to see the coronation, not a bus on which the Queen rode.
discrepancy: The bus carried members of the public to see the coronation; presenting the Queen as its upper-deck passenger materially substitutes the event participants.

name: nasa-pillars-near-duplicate

anchor.statement: The image visibly shows the characteristic pillar-shaped nebular scene known as the Pillars of Creation.

claim: The image is the near-infrared Pillars of Creation capture released for the Eagle Nebula.
hypothesis: An official NASA reference image can confirm whether the input is the same capture.
expected_information: A direct comparison with an official reference that establishes capture identity and absence of material changes.
exact_text: The input and official NASA reference are near-duplicate near-infrared captures of the Pillars of Creation, with no structural, color, or content differences.
assessment_rationale: The official same-capture comparison supports the sole high-salience claim and shows no material discrepancy.

name: monarch-antarctica-ecology

anchor.statement: Monarch butterflies are visibly presented among ice, penguins, and conifer branches in an Antarctic scene.

claim: The image presents monarch butterflies as naturally occurring in an Antarctic habitat.
hypothesis: Authoritative ecological evidence can determine whether butterflies naturally occur in Antarctica.
expected_information: A fetched ecological source that directly resolves the species-to-habitat relation.
exact_text: No, there are no butterflies in Antarctica. The only insect is the wingless midge, a tiny insect that lives in amongst the moss and lichens on the edges of the continent and which can freeze solid over the winter months, yet come back to life in summer to breed.
assessment_rationale: The ecological range evidence directly contradicts the visibly anchored Antarctica habitat relation.
discrepancy: The image places monarch butterflies in a natural Antarctic habitat outside their documented range, creating a decisive ecological contradiction.
